claim: The age dynamics of sexual partnership formation determine patterns of sexually transmitted disease transmission.
source: The age dynamics of sexual partnership formation determine patterns of sexually transmitted disease transmission and have long been a focus of researchers studying human immunodeficiency virus.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract and introduction, representing scientific consensus in the field.

claim: Data on self-reported sexual partner age distributions are available from a variety of sources.
source: Data on self-reported sexual partner age distributions are available from a variety of sources.

claim: Distributional regression with a sinh-arcsinh distribution replicated observed partner age distributions most accurately across three geographically diverse data sets.
source: We found that distributional regression with a sinh-arcsinh distribution replicated observed partner age distributions most accurately across three geographically diverse data sets.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study, supported by ELPD and QQ RMSE comparisons presented in Tables 4 and 5.
